thread.title: 2019 Outlook: Will It A Lost Year For Apple Stock? | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: 2019 Outlook: Will It A Lost Year For Apple Stock? | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Apple stock is poised to end 2018 about where it started the year. It had been up as much as 25%, soaring past a market value of $1 trillion in early August, but then investors soured on the stock amid slowing iPhone sales.
X With 2018 looking like a lost year for Apple ( AAPL ) stock, investors are wondering what's in store for 2019. At least one analyst thinks Apple stock won't return to favor until late in the year.
Loup Ventures managing partner Gene Munster thinks Apple stock will be in the doghouse until late 2019 when investors begin to accept Apple more as a services company than a hardware company. Apple might not return to its $1 trillion valuation milestone in the new year, Munster said.
"I don't know if we'll get back to it in 2019, but in 2020 and beyond we will get back to it and go measurably higher," Munster said. "It's going to take four quarters for investors to get their bearings around this new reporting, which gets us to the September-October time frame next year."

Please contact customer service CLOSE Apple stock tumbled in early November when the company announced that it would no longer release hardware unit sales. Investors took that as a sign that iPhone unit sales would soon turn negative.
Apple's 12th-generation handsets have not provided the sales boost investors had expected. In particular, the midrange iPhone XR has disappointed.
In lieu of hardware unit data, Apple said it will provide profit margins on hardware and services.
Apple Stock Hit With 'One-Two Punch' Apple stock has taken a "one-two punch" from slowing iPhone sales and the company's lack of transparency, Wedbush Securities analyst Daniel Ives said. Investors are now wondering if the iPhone growth story is dead, he added.
Apple miscalculated pricing on the iPhone XR and may need to get more aggressive on promotions and marketing, Ives said. On the plus side, Apple's installed base of 750 million active iPhones is fairly loyal, he said. It's only a matter of time before they upgrade to new iPhones.
"The retention rate has been pretty strong," Ives said. "It's not like the average iPhone customer is going to Samsung and Android."
The transition to 5G cellular networks could provide a major upgrade opportunity for Apple, said Munster.
"5G rollout in earnest in the U.S. isn't probably until 2020 or 2021," he said. "Apple won't be first to the party, but they will arrive in plenty of time to capitalize on 5G."
Apple will want to make sure the new networks are reliable and the components are working properly before it dives into 5G handsets, Munster said.
Apple Streaming Video Service Seen Making Headlines In 2019 To make up for softness in iPhone sales , Apple is focusing on services and wearables.
The big services story for Apple in 2019 will be the expected launch of a streaming video service to compete with the likes of Netflix ( NFLX ) and Amazon ( AMZN ) Prime Video.
Apple's video offering is likely to debut as a stand-alone service in the second half of the year, Ives said. It has ordered TV series from such big-name producers as Steven Spielberg, J.J. Abrams and M. Night Shyamalan.
To compete, Apple will need to ramp up its spending on video content from the current $1 billion to $1.5 billion a year to maybe $4 billion or $5 billion a year for the next couple of years, Ives said. Apple might decide to acquire an independent movie studio like A24, he said.
Apple could take a more measured approach to its video service, Munster said. The Cupertino, Calif.-based company could start the video offering as an extra to Apple Music subscribers. It might even offer some content for free to build awareness, he said.
On the wearables front, Apple is pushing AirPods wireless earbuds, the Apple Watch smartwatch and Beats headphones. Apple is rumored to be coming out with second-generation AirPods in early 2019.
Could Augmented Reality Glasses Be On The Way? Meanwhile, some Apple watchers say the company is overdue to come out with its next big thing.
"There's a void from a product perspective for investors to get excited about," Ives said.
That next big thing could be augmented reality glasses, Ives and Munster said. Apple has taken baby steps in augmented reality by adding the technology to its mobile operating system, iOS, and devices like the iPhone. It also has acquired small companies working on promising AR technology.
If it could overlay digital information into a person's field of view with eyeglasses, it could be a game changer for the company, analysts say.
The key will be concealing the technology in a fashionable set of eyewear. That's something no company has yet to accomplish.
In the short term, however, Apple has some major uncertainty ahead.
"They're going through a bad storm with a lot of turbulence and investors are just trying to figure out how this flight ends," Ives said.
